newsitem.title: USA: AAA urges fed action to avoid any gas price hikes.
newsitem.headline: AAA urges fed action to avoid any gas price hikes.

text.p: The American Automobile Association urged the U.S. Energy Department on Thursday to set minimum inventory levels for the nation's oil industry to avert possible price spikes and supply disruptions.
In a letter to Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary, the association said an inventory floor was needed to protect against a harsh winter or unexpected changes in the market.
The letter follows the federation's release on Tuesday of its latest fuel price survey, which showed a 17 cent increase in December self-serve regular unleaded gasoline from year-ago levels.
The price, nearly $1.29 a gallon, is 1 cent higher than November and just a touch below highs hit last summer.

"By keeping gasoline and oil inventories at such low levels, refiners are leaving the traveling public vulnerable to the vagaries of the global market," AAA President Robert L. Darbelnet said in the letter.
In the last year, oil refineries have tried to minimize stocks to free-up capital in a time of poor profit margins.
AAA said crude oil inventories, for the first since before the 1973-74 Arab oil embargo, are below 300 million barrels.
Gasoline inventories have also fallen below 190 million barrels -- a critical threshold below which many industry analysts consider prices more vulnernable to spikes.
"Low inventories have a direct effect on consumers. These tight fuel supplies can lead to another run-up in pump prices like the 18-cent per gallon jump last spring," Darbelnet said.
Much of that run-up was due in part to low stocks in anticipation of Iraqi oil returning to the market in 1995 and outages at several refineries in California.
